analysis.title: "Nobody Really Knows What To Worry About": Goldman's Privorotsky Sees A "Painful Year-End Rally" That Nobody Will Be Able To Chase
key_insights: Privorotsky (GS Delta One, EMEA) says the AI bear case is circular. One camp argues power and data center capacity cannot support 2027 spending, so picks-and-shovels growth rolls over. The other argues compute will be overproduced and rental economics will collapse. Both camps conclude multiples compress.

Hyperscaler cloud demand is not in dispute. Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%. Combined growth for Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft was 54% y/y in Q3, the sixth straight quarter of acceleration (GS GIR).

Returns on capital are the open question. Privorotsky cites negative FCF, equity raises and rising leverage needs. Coppersmith says 2027 hyperscaler capex is expected at $1.2 trillion and aggregate free cash flow turned negative in Q3.

The article's author notes that $1.2 trillion of 2027 capex against negative FCF implies the spending is funded in the bond market. It cites an AI off-balance-sheet obligation figure of $4.1 trillion.
Coppersmith's bull rebuttal: Oracle plans about $220 billion of AI infrastructure spending but expects to raise just $20bn through 2030, with customers and suppliers helping foot the bill.

Intel fell 29% on Friday after a 'surprisingly severe PC correction'. Privorotsky says the warning was more about consumer PCs, margins and manufacturing than AI demand, but the market traded it as an AI casualty.

Amazon, described as a well-owned position, went from down 7% pre-market to closing 1.4% lower despite FCF concerns. Kioxia fell 15% on Monday, which Privorotsky says shows the rebound is not indiscriminate.

Positioning: GS systematic L/S performance estimate fell 2.17% in a week, the worst weekly drawdown since Dec '23. Fundamental L/S nets recovered only to the 7th percentile, largely through index short covering. Single stocks were net sold for a 7th straight week, while macro products were net bought for a second week.

Privorotsky's verdict is that sentiment and positioning have been reset. He describes October as wholesale de-grossing, with momentum unwinding, most-shorted names squeezing, and defensives and quality outperforming while AI multiples compress.

Coppersmith disagrees that the reset is done. October saw the largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021, but risk appetite is not at levels that signal a contrarian buy. Gross exposure is still 314% (97th percentile over 5 years), so there is fuel for more volatility.
After the 11 largest risk appetite declines since 2005, S&P outcomes ranged from -17% to +7% a month out.

Privorotsky's call: he expects a painful year-end rally, with markets under-owned, poorly participated in and impossible to chase. He thinks events must clear before risk is added. UBS also warns of a year-end squeeze with shorts near records.

Week-ahead events: US midterms (Tuesday), Treasury QRA (Wednesday), AMD earnings (Tuesday), payrolls (Friday, consensus about +65K, unemployment 4.2%). Privorotsky says the QRA 'feels potentially underappreciated'. Duration relief from smaller long-end auctions, buybacks or more bills could help duration and growth equities.
BoE: Thursday's 25bp hike to 4% is almost fully priced. Privorotsky leans toward the market overpricing the three to four further hikes priced over the next year.
Oil is down 3% on Iran talks via Qatar and is below $100. Privorotsky says it is unclear whether the diplomatic window survives the elections.

The article's author (not Goldman) suspects any year-end rally is a gift to sell into, citing negative hyperscaler FCF, 97th percentile gross leverage and a 2027 capex bill landing on the bond market while the Fed is hiking.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is undeniable. Cloud growth accelerated for a sixth straight quarter to 54%, and nothing in the hyperscaler results suggested spending intentions were weakening. Oracle expects to raise only $20bn through 2030, with customers and suppliers sharing the cost.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow turned negative in Q3 and 2027 capex is expected at $1.2 trillion, with funding falling on the bond market. Equity raises and leverage needs raise questions about returns on the next trillion of investment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Treasury duration relief at Wednesday's QRA could ease the funding concern. A hyperscaler FCF turnaround would undercut the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky expects a painful year-end rally. Nets are at the 7th percentile, sentiment is washed out, and the post-midterm period has historically been positive for equities. UBS also sees shorts near records.
tension_points.bear_case: Coppersmith says risk appetite is not at contrarian-buy levels and gross exposure is 314% (97th percentile), so more volatility remains possible. S&P outcomes after large risk appetite drops ranged from -17% to +7%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Privorotsky wants the midterms, Treasury QRA, AMD earnings and Friday's payrolls cleared before risk is added. A poor outcome in those events would delay or break the rally thesis.
